newsitem.title: USA: Blue-chip stocks extend run into record territory.
newsitem.headline: Blue-chip stocks extend run into record territory.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks extended their run into record ground Monday as the prospects that the Federal Reserve will keep interest rates steady renewed Wall Street's confidence in the outlook for stocks.

At 1 p.m. EDT, the Dow Jones Industrial Average was up 41.43 points at 5,879.95, surpassing Friday's record close of 5,838.52. In the broader market, advancing issues beat declines 12-9 on moderate volume of 226 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Nasdaq Composite index was up 7.35 at 1,196.02. The American Stock Exchange index was up 0.35 to 570.61.

Analysts said the market got a boost from Dean Witter's announcement that it was raising the percentage of stocks held in its basic asset allocation model to 60 percent from 55 percent, citing diminished risk from higher interest rates over the near-term.
"Interest rate risks may not have been eliminated but they've certainly been deferred," said Peter Canelo, chief investment strategist at Dean Witter.
The firm cut cash to 20 percent in the model and left bonds steady at 20 percent.

The brokerage house's decision was another indication that the Dow industrials, which bounded higher Friday after a surprisingly tame Consumer Price Index for August, may be poised to take a long-delayed run at the 6,000-point level.

"The fear in the market is dissipating as we move higher," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd. "We have momentum carried over from last week and 6,000 is obviously the next target," he said.
Technology stocks set the pace on both the NYSE and Nasdaq, with chip makers Intel Corp., Micron Technology Inc., and Motorola Inc. all posting gains.
America Online Inc. rose 3/4 to 27-3/4 in its first day of trading after switching its shares to an NYSE listing from Nasdaq.
General Motors Corp. gained 1 to 50-1/4 on a report that the company was considering selling its Hughes Electronics unit.

A GM spokesman confirmed the company was reviewing several options for the unit but noted that it had said as much in a Securities and Exchange Commission filing last April. No timetable has been set for choosing or implementing any of the strategic alternatives, he said.
While overall sentiment may have improved, Wall Street continued to punish the companies that disappointed the market.
Glenayre Technologies Inc. fell 13-1/8 to 20-1/8 after announcing late Friday that its third quarter earnings would fell short of year-ago levels.
Anadigics Inc., which also warned investors late Friday about its third quarter outlook, fell 6-5/8 to 22-7/8.
